description: Public development fixtures for evaluating evidence-grounded KQA questionnaire critique. This corpus is not a held-out performance set.

cases.brief: Understand how customers use the mobile checkout and whether payment feels secure.

questions.label: How easy and secure was checkout?

gold.rationale: Ease and perceived security are separate constructs and may have different answers.

cases.brief: Learn about the last online order experience.

questions.label: Thinking about your most recent online order, how easy or difficult was it to find the item you wanted?

cases.brief: Learn whether the new weekly planning meeting is useful.

questions.label: How much has the excellent new weekly planning meeting improved your productivity?

gold.rationale: Excellent presupposes a positive evaluation and the question assumes productivity improved.

cases.brief: Measure recent use of the local library service.

questions.label: How often do you use the library?

gold.rationale: Recent is not defined for respondents and the frequency categories have no common time window.

cases.brief: Find which sessions attendees visited at a three-day conference.

questions.label: List every session you attended, with its start time and room.

gold.rationale: Reconstructing every session plus exact time and room across three days is a high and unnecessary recall burden for the stated purpose.

cases.brief: Understand how quickly a support request was handled.

gold.rationale: Boundary values such as exactly 2 or 4 hours fit two options.

cases.brief: Learn which device people use for the service, including less common devices.

gold.rationale: The options exclude desktop and other plausible devices despite the brief requiring less common devices to be represented.

cases.brief: Measure satisfaction with a training session. Include a neutral answer so respondents are not forced toward satisfaction or dissatisfaction.

questions.label: How satisfied were you with the training?

gold.rationale: The brief explicitly requires a neutral answer, but the four-point scale offers none.

cases.brief: Understand whether the appointment booking flow was easy to use.

questions.label: What is your medical diagnosis and medication list?

gold.rationale: The requested health details are sensitive and do not inform the stated usability purpose.

cases.brief: Help a person reflect on what support they would like next.

questions.label: What, if anything, would you like to do next?

cases.brief: Identify the most important blocker to completing a task, including blockers outside the common categories below.

gold.rationale: The brief explicitly asks to capture blockers beyond these common categories, but the fixed-choice item has no unlisted response.

cases.brief: Learn about customer use of a subscription service.

questions.label: Which subscription plan do you currently use?

cases.brief: Find one improvement to the onboarding process.

questions.label: How good or poor was onboarding?

gold.rationale: The second item repeats the first rating without adding a distinct purpose, increasing burden before the requested improvement question.

cases.brief: Learn whether customers could access the service in their preferred language and what support was missing.

questions.label: How satisfied are you with the service?

gold.rationale: The questionnaire does not ask about preferred language access or missing support, both explicit information needs in the brief.

cases.brief: Reflect on priorities for the coming month.

questions.label: What would you most like to make time for in the coming month?

cases.brief: Understand whether people have enough time for their current workload.

gold.rationale: The question does not state enough time for what, such as core tasks, breaks, or development; respondents may answer different constructs.

cases.brief: Collect local priorities for an open-ended consultation.

questions.label: What should decision-makers consider before deciding?
